what: A trace of one card's passage across a superpipeline board, published so the post beside it can be checked rather than believed.
completeness: This trace covers the card through to its final stage.

card.title: The lab never closes — introducing Super Jackfruit Labs

notIncluded: Matrix room ids, event ids or message content
prompts, which may quote private material

howToReadThis.routing: An agent did not receive a stage because of its name. The board matched the stage's required capability against the capabilities the agent declares, which is exact string equality — so the `capabilities` field beside each run is the reason that agent got that stage.
howToReadThis.gates: A human gate parks the card until a person answers. superpipeline refuses to let the agent that produced a gate resolve it, which is why `producedBy` and `decidedBy` are both recorded here.
howToReadThis.limits: This records what the board observed. It is not a claim that the work is good, and a `completed` outcome means the run ended cleanly, not that it was right.
howToReadThis.repeatedStages: A stage may appear more than once. superpipeline marks a run `completed` when it ends cleanly, whether or not it produced the intended result, so a repeated stage usually means an earlier run finished without doing the work — it stopped on a condition it was told to respect, or was sent back. For a repeated stage, the last run is the one whose result stands.
